findings.heading: Download offline handbook / Tải sách ngoại tuyến
findings.proposition: The English gives the actual download instruction for the offline handbook: right-click the link https://github.com/appliedepi/epirhandbook/raw/main/offline_long/index.html and select "Save link as" (Cmd+click on Mac, press-and-hold on mobile), plus the note that a screen of raw HTML means the instructions were not followed. The Vietnamese section contains no download link and no download instruction at all.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader reaches the end of the section titled "Tải sách ngoại tuyến" (Download offline handbook) with no way to download it: there is no URL and no procedure, so the section cannot be acted on.

findings.heading: Download offline handbook / Tải sách ngoại tuyến
findings.proposition: The Vietnamese bullet list carries a fourth bullet, "Cài đặt package **appliedepidata** của chúng tôi trong đó chứa tất cả các dữ liệu minh họa (quy trình cài đặt được mô tả bên dưới)", instructing the reader to install the appliedepidata package as a step of preparing for offline use. The English list of offline-use considerations has three bullets and does not include this item.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader is told installing appliedepidata is part of the offline-handbook preparation checklist, which the English does not claim; if the bullet list later drifts from the English source, the two versions give different offline preparation steps.

findings.heading: Case linelist / Dữ liệu linelist
findings.proposition: The Vietnamese prose beside the linelist_cleaned_rds chunk claims "Điều này đảm bảo bạn sẽ có ít việc phải làm khi làm sạch số liệu sau khi nhập số liệu vào R" (this ensures you will have only minimal cleaning to do after importing the data into R). The English text beside the same object says only that the .rds file preserves column classes and is used for all other linelist pages; it makes the minimal-cleaning claim only for the malaria dataset, not for the linelist.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader is led to expect the cleaned linelist .rds needs almost no further cleaning, a guarantee the English does not make for this dataset, so they may skip the cleaning steps the Cleaning data chapter still expects.

findings.heading: Flexdashboard
findings.proposition: The English states that the Flexdashboard files are R Markdown/HTML source files rather than example datasets, that they are therefore not part of the appliedepidata package, and that they must be downloaded directly from Github. The Vietnamese sentence says only "Dưới đây là các liên kết đến tệp được dùng trong chương Dashboards với R Markdown" and drops all three points.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader may search appliedepidata with get_data() for the flexdashboard files, find nothing, and not understand that these files are only available by direct Github download.

findings.heading: Contact Tracing / Truy vết tiếp xúc
findings.proposition: The English states "This data is not part of **appliedepidata**" about the Go.Data contact tracing data. The Vietnamese sentence omits that clause entirely and goes straight from the Go.Data attribution to the download links.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader may try appliedepidata::get_data() for the contact tracing datasets and fail, without being told that these data live outside the package and must come from the WHO Github links.

findings.heading: Time series and outbreak detection / Chuỗi thời gian và phát hiện ổ dịch
findings.proposition: The English points the reader to the Time series and outbreak detection page at time_series.qmd. The Vietnamese link targets epidemic_models.vn.qmd, a different chapter; the Vietnamese time series chapter exists at chapters/time_series.vn.qmd and other Vietnamese chapters (moving_average.vn.qmd:110, dates.vn.qmd:618) link to it under exactly that name.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader following the link is sent to the epidemic modelling chapter, or to a broken link, instead of the time series and outbreak detection chapter where the campylobacter and German weather data are actually used.
